summary: This article explains how bookbinders once folded, sewed, and covered books entirely by hand, and how binders and illuminators in the Islamic world turned plain books into lasting works of art.
introduce: Show the title “The Art of Bookbinding” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a set of folded pages that will be sewn into a book
a skilled worker who makes things carefully by hand
a thin, strong string used for sewing

challengeTerms.def: to decorate a manuscript's pages with gold and bright colors
to cover something with a thin layer of gold
someone who learns a skilled craft by working with an experienced master

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a handmade book can be a work of art, not just a way to read? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a durable, well-made cover protected a book over many years.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review signature, craftsman, and thread, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses illuminate, gild, and apprentice to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
